alerts.summary: Metro-district debt service can add 40-70+ mills to the effective tax rate without appearing in the list price.
alerts.analysis: Metro-district mill levies are a recurring cost the listing never headlines. Pull the property's total mill levy and the district's debt profile from the transparency portal before pricing an offer; a 60-mill district on a $700k home is roughly $2,900/yr above a comparable non-district home.

alerts.summary: Larimer County is EPA radon Zone 1: testing is the norm, not an exotic ask.
alerts.analysis: Radon testing during inspection is standard practice in Larimer County and sellers must disclose known radon history (C.R.S. 38-35.7-109). A failed test is a negotiation item: active mitigation typically runs $1,500-$2,500 — ask for it as a credit or repair, never absorb it silently.

alerts.summary: Wildfire-exposed foothills properties can be uninsurable or carry premiums that break the monthly budget.
alerts.analysis: For any property at moderate-or-higher wildfire risk, obtain an actual insurance quote BEFORE the inspection window closes — non-renewal patterns in the foothills mean the FAIR plan (last-resort coverage, higher cost, lower limits) may be the only option, and lenders require proof of insurability to close.

alerts.summary: Active or permitted oil/gas locations near the parcel affect health, financing, insurance, and resale.
alerts.analysis: Query the ECMC well database for active, permitted, or abandoned wells within the setback-relevant radius of the parcel. New-development setbacks are 2,000 ft (Rule 604), but existing wells can sit far closer to existing homes; verify plugging status for abandoned wells and disclose findings to the inspector.
